q: Which scientist proposed the Law of Triads for classifying elements?
e: Döbereiner arranged similar elements in groups of three (triads) where the middle element's atomic mass was roughly the average of the other two.

q: Who proposed the Law of Octaves in 1866?
e: John Newlands noticed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first when arranged by increasing atomic mass.

q: Newlands' Law of Octaves was found to be applicable only up to which element?
e: The Law of Octaves held true only up to Calcium (atomic mass 40); heavier elements did not follow the pattern.

q: Mendeleev's Periodic Law was based on which fundamental property of elements?
e: Mendeleev stated that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.

q: How many elements were known when Mendeleev started developing his periodic table?
e: At the time of Mendeleev's work, 63 elements were known (compared to 56 for Newlands).

q: Who proposed the Modern Periodic Law, and on what atomic property is it based?
e: In 1913, Henry Moseley showed that atomic number is a more fundamental property than atomic mass.

q: How many periods (horizontal rows) and groups (vertical columns) are present in the Modern Periodic Table?
e: The Modern Periodic Table consists of 7 horizontal periods and 18 vertical groups.

q: Elements of Group 18 (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn) in the Modern Periodic Table are known as:
e: Group 18 elements have completely filled outer shells and are chemically inert, called noble gases.

q: Metals in Group 1 (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) are commonly called:
e: Group 1 metals form strong alkalis with water and are known as alkali metals.

q: Elements of Group 17 (F, Cl, Br, I) are collectively called:
e: Group 17 elements (F, Cl, Br, I) are known as halogens (salt-formers) with 7 valence electrons.

q: How many elements are present in Group 1 of the Modern Periodic Table (including Hydrogen)? [JAC 2020]
o: 7 (H, Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr)
e: Across periods 1 to 7, Group 1 contains 7 elements: H, Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, and Fr.

q: How many elements are present in the first period of the Modern Periodic Table?
e: The 1st period fills the K shell (capacity 2) and contains only 2 elements: H and He.

q: How many elements are present in each of the 2nd and 3rd periods?
e: Both the 2nd and 3rd periods contain 8 elements each.

q: How many elements are present in each of the 4th and 5th periods?
e: The 4th and 5th periods are long periods containing 18 elements each.

q: Which electronic configuration among the following belongs to a noble gas? [JAC 2024]
e: Configuration 2, 8 (Neon, Z=10) has a completely filled outermost shell and represents a noble gas.

q: Which of the following elements will have the same number of valence electrons as Lithium? [JAC 2024]
e: Both Lithium (2,1) and Potassium (2,8,8,1) belong to Group 1 and have 1 valence electron.

q: Why do all elements belonging to the same group have similar chemical properties? [JAC 2020]
o: They have the same number of valence electrons in their outermost shell
e: Chemical properties depend on valence electrons, and all elements in a given group possess the same valence electron count.

q: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a shell of principal number n is given by:
e: Maximum electron capacity of shell n is 2n² (2 for K, 8 for L, 18 for M, 32 for N).

q: What does the zig-zag borderline in the Modern Periodic Table separate?
o: Metals from non-metals (with metalloids lying along the border)
e: The zig-zag diagonal separates metals on the left from non-metals on the right, with metalloids (B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te, Po) along the line.

q: Mendeleev predicted undiscovered elements leaving gaps. "Eka-aluminium" was later discovered and named:
e: Mendeleev's Eka-boron became Scandium, Eka-aluminium became Gallium, and Eka-silicon became Germanium.

q: Which element discovered later matched Mendeleev's predicted "Eka-silicon"?
e: Germanium closely matched every property Mendeleev predicted for Eka-silicon.

q: How does atomic radius (atomic size) vary on moving from left to right across a period?
e: Moving across a period increases nuclear charge while electrons enter the same shell, pulling electrons closer and decreasing atomic size.

q: On going down a group in the periodic table, what happens to the atomic size?
o: Increases (as new shells are added at each step)
e: Down a group, each new period adds a new electron shell, increasing distance from the nucleus and thus increasing atomic size.

q: Across a period from left to right, how does metallic character change?
e: Increased effective nuclear charge across a period holds valence electrons more tightly, decreasing tendency to lose electrons (metallic character).

q: Moving down a group, how does metallic character vary?
o: Increases (outermost electrons are further away and lost easily)
e: Down a group, larger atomic radius allows valence electrons to be lost more easily, so metallic character increases.

q: Magnesium (atomic number 12) is located in which period and group of the Modern Periodic Table?
e: Mg has configuration 2,8,2: 3 shells place it in Period 3, and 2 valence electrons place it in Group 2.

q: Which set contains ONLY metalloids (semimetals)?
e: Boron, silicon, and germanium exhibit properties intermediate between metals and non-metals.

q: Which element is the most electronegative element in the periodic table?
e: Fluorine (Group 17, Period 2) has the strongest tendency to attract shared electrons, making it the most electronegative element.

q: Among the elements of Period 3 (Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl), which atom has the LARGEST atomic radius?
e: Because atomic size decreases from left to right across Period 3, Sodium (leftmost) has the largest radius.

q: Which anomaly remained unresolved in Mendeleev's periodic table?
o: Fixed position of Hydrogen, position of isotopes, and inverted atomic mass pairs like Co before Ni
e: Anomalous position of hydrogen, isotopes having different masses, and atomic mass inversions (Co before Ni) were Mendeleev's key limitations.

q: In Döbereiner's triad containing Lithium (atomic mass 6.9) and Potassium (39.0), which element is in the middle?
e: The mean of Li (6.9) and K (39.0) is ~23.0, matching Sodium (Na). Other classic triads are Ca-Sr-Ba and Cl-Br-I.

q: Using Döbereiner's triad rule for Cl (35.5) and I (127), what is the approximate atomic mass of middle element Bromine (Br)?
e: Average = (35.5 + 127)/2 = 81.25, close to Bromine's actual mass of 79.9 u.

q: Why did Mendeleev place Cobalt (mass 58.9) before Nickel (mass 58.7), and how did the Modern Periodic Table resolve it?
o: Modern table uses atomic number (Co Z=27, Ni Z=28), automatically placing Co before Ni
e: Atomic numbers increase naturally from Co (27) to Ni (28), resolving the atomic mass anomaly completely.

q: Why are isotopes like Cl-35 and Cl-37 placed in the SAME slot in the Modern Periodic Table?
o: Both have the exact same atomic number (Z = 17) and chemical properties
e: Isotopes share the same atomic number (proton count) and valence electrons, placing them in the exact same position.

q: Which statement highlights a limitation of Newlands' Law of Octaves?
o: He placed Co and Ni in the same slot with halogens (F, Cl, Br) while placing similar Fe far away
He left gaps for noble gases
e: Newlands forced Co and Ni together into the halogen column and placed Fe far from Co/Ni, while assuming only 56 elements existed.

q: How does valency (with respect to hydrogen or maximum combining capacity) vary across Period 2 (Li to Ne) or Period 3 (Na to Ar)?
o: First increases from 1 to 4, then decreases from 4 to 0
e: Across a short period, valency rises 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 (Groups 1, 2, 13, 14) and then falls 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 (Groups 15, 16, 17, 18).

q: An element has electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. Find its period, group, and valency:
e: Three shells → Period 3; 7 valence electrons → Group 10+7 = 17; Valency = 8 - 7 = 1 (Chlorine).

q: For main-group elements having 3 to 8 valence electrons in Periods 2 and 3, how is their Group number calculated?
e: For 1 or 2 valence electrons, Group = 1 or 2; for 3 to 8 valence electrons in short periods, Group = 10 + valence electrons (13 to 18).

q: When noble gases (He, Ne, Ar) were discovered late, why could they fit cleanly without disturbing the existing Mendeleev table?
o: Placed in a separate new group (Zero group / Group 18)
e: Because noble gases are inert and have 0 valency, they were placed smoothly in a new Zero group (Group 18) without altering earlier placements.

q: In Period 3 (Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl, Ar), classify which are metals, metalloid, and non-metals:
o: Na, Mg, Al are metals; Si is a metalloid; P, S, Cl, Ar are non-metals
Only Cl and Ar are non-metals
e: In Period 3, Na, Mg, Al are metals; Si is a metalloid; and P, S, Cl, Ar are non-metals.

q: Among Na, Mg, Al, S, and Cl, which elements form the most basic oxide and the most acidic oxide respectively?
o: Cl most basic, Na most acidic
Na forms the most basic oxide and Cl forms the most acidic oxide
e: Moving left to right, oxides change from strongly basic (Na2O) → amphoteric (Al2O3) → strongly acidic (SO3/Cl2O7).

q: In Mendeleev's periodic table, how were the general oxide formulas of Group I and Group IV written?
e: Mendeleev grouped elements by oxide and hydride formulas: R2O for Group I and RO2 for Group IV.

q: Which atomic number corresponds to an element chemically similar to Chlorine (Z = 17)? [NCERT]
e: Z=9 (Fluorine: 2,7) shares the same 7 valence electrons and Group 17 properties as Chlorine (2,8,7).

q: Element A has atomic number 12 and element B has atomic number 17. What is the formula of the compound formed between them?
e: A (valency 2) and B (valency 1) combine in a 1:2 ratio to form AB2.

q: Which element in Group 16 (O, S, Se, Te, Po) is the most electronegative and non-metallic?
e: Non-metallic character and electronegativity decrease down a group, making Oxygen at the top the most electronegative.

q: Arrange Period 2 elements O, N, C, B, Be in INCREASING order of atomic radius:
e: Atomic radius shrinks from Be to O across Period 2, so the increasing order is O < N < C < B < Be.

q: Among alkali metals Li, Na, K, Rb, and Cs, which has the largest atomic radius and highest electropositive reactivity?
e: Down Group 1, atomic radius and ease of electron loss increase, making Caesium the largest and most reactive stable alkali metal.

q: Even though Helium (Z=2) has 2 valence electrons like Be and Mg, why is it placed in Group 18 instead of Group 2?
o: Its K shell (capacity 2) is completely filled, making it chemically inert like other noble gases
e: Helium's first and only K shell is completely saturated with 2 electrons (duplet), giving it the chemical inertness of Group 18.

q: Which statement accurately describes Silicon (Z = 14)?
o: A metalloid in Period 3, Group 14 with valency 4
e: Silicon (2,8,4) lies in Period 3, Group 14 along the metalloid line, having valency 4.

q: Element M forms a chloride MCl2, a solid with high melting point. Which element from Period 3 does M resemble?
e: Formula MCl2 and high-melting ionic solid indicate a Group 2 divalent metal like Magnesium.

q: An element X in Period 3 forms an amphoteric oxide X2O3. Identify element X:
e: Aluminium (Period 3, Group 13) forms the amphoteric oxide Al2O3.

q: In what order did Newlands arrange the 56 known elements in his Octaves table (from H to Th)?
e: Döbereiner, Newlands, and Mendeleev all arranged elements in order of increasing atomic masses.

q: Where are non-metals predominantly located in the Modern Periodic Table?
o: Top right-hand side (upper right of zig-zag line)
e: Non-metals occupy the upper right-hand side of the Modern Periodic Table, to the right of the metalloid zig-zag line.

q: Which element in Period 2 has valency 4 and forms the backbone of organic compounds?
e: Carbon (Z=6, configuration 2,4) is in Period 2, Group 14 with valency 4.

q: Which element has a total of two shells, both of which are completely filled with electrons? [NCERT]
e: Neon (Z=10) has K=2, L=8, so both shells are completely filled.

q: Which element has a total of three shells, with 4 electrons in its valence shell? [NCERT]
e: Configuration 2, 8, 4 (three shells, 4 valence electrons, Z=14) belongs to Silicon.

q: Which element has twice as many electrons in its second shell as in its first shell? [NCERT]
e: The first shell holds 2 electrons; twice that in the second shell is 4, giving configuration 2, 4 — Carbon.

q: Oxygen (Z=8) and Sulphur (Z=16) are placed in the same group (Group 16) because:
o: Both have 6 valence electrons in their outermost shells (2,6 and 2,8,6)
e: Both have 6 valence electrons, giving them the same valency (2) and similar chemical behaviour.

q: Why did the discovery of isotopes pose a challenge to Mendeleev's Periodic Law?
o: Isotopes of an element have identical chemical properties yet different atomic masses, demanding separate slots by mass
e: An atomic-mass-based law would require placing isotopes of different masses in different slots despite identical chemistry.

q: Why does Hydrogen have an anomalous/unique position at the top of the Modern Periodic Table?
o: It resembles both Group 1 alkali metals (forms H⁺) and Group 17 halogens (diatomic H2, forms H⁻)
e: With 1 valence electron (1 short of duplet), hydrogen mirrors alkali metals (H⁺, oxides/halides) as well as halogens (diatomic H2, covalent compounds).

q: Three elements X, Y, and Z have atomic numbers 6, 10, and 14 respectively. Which two will show similar chemical properties?
e: Both X (2,4) and Z (2,8,4) have 4 valence electrons and belong to Group 14; Y (2,8) is inert Neon.

q: Element A (Z = 19) reacts with element B (Z = 8). Identify the formula and bonding of the compound:
e: A (K: 2,8,8,1) transfers 1 electron per atom and B (O: 2,6) accepts 2 electrons, forming ionic A2B.

q: Among Group 2 elements Be (Z=4), Mg (Z=12), and Ca (Z=20), which has the smallest and largest atom respectively?
o: Be smallest (2 shells), Ca largest (4 shells)
e: Adding shells down the group makes Be (2 shells) smallest and Ca (4 shells) largest.

q: An atom P has 3 electrons in its third (M) shell. Find its atomic number and the formula of its chloride:
e: Configuration 2,8,3 gives Z=13 (Al) with valency 3, so its chloride formula is PCl3.

q: Element X has configuration 2, 8, 6. Identify its period and the formula of its compound with hydrogen:
e: Three shells → Period 3; 6 valence electrons → valency 2, giving hydride H2X (H2S).

q: Arrange Li (Z=3), C (Z=6), and F (Z=9) in INCREASING order of non-metallic character:
e: Across Period 2, non-metallic character increases from left to right: Li < C < F.

q: Elements Li (7), Na (23), and K (39) form a triad. Check the arithmetic mean of Li and K:
e: (7 + 39) / 2 = 23, matching the atomic mass of Sodium exactly.

q: Element X lies in Group 16 and Period 2. Find its atomic number, valency, and formula with Sodium (Na):
e: Period 2 (2 shells) and Group 16 (6 valence electrons) gives configuration 2,6 (Z=8, Oxygen), valency 2, forming Na2O.

q: What is the decreasing order of chemical reactivity (tendency to gain an electron) among halogens F, Cl, Br?
e: Down Group 17, increasing atomic radius weakens attraction for an incoming electron, so non-metallic reactivity decreases: F > Cl > Br.

q: Why does reactivity INCREASE down Group 1 (Li < Na < K) whereas it DECREASES down Group 17 (F > Cl > Br)?
o: Larger size down Group 1 eases electron loss, whereas smaller size at top of Group 17 favours electron gain
e: Metals react by losing electrons (favoured by larger radius down the group), while non-metals react by gaining electrons (favoured by smaller radius at top).

q: Element M has atomic number 11. What is the formula of its oxide and its effect on litmus when dissolved in water?
o: M2O, turns red litmus blue (forms strong alkali MOH)
e: M (Z=11, Sodium) forms basic oxide M2O (Na2O), dissolving to give alkali NaOH that turns red litmus blue.

q: In Mendeleev's table, Silicon lies in Group IV. Using Mendeleev's general notation, what is the formula of its oxide?
e: Group IV elements exhibit valency 4 towards oxygen, corresponding to Mendeleev's general oxide formula RO2.

q: Elements A, B, and C belong to the same period and form basic, amphoteric, and acidic oxides respectively. Arrange their atomic numbers in INCREASING order:
e: Across a period (increasing Z), oxides progress from basic (left) → amphoteric (middle) → acidic (right), so A < B < C.

q: Which element among Na (11), Al (13), Si (14), and P (15) has the MAXIMUM number of valence electrons?
e: Phosphorus (2,8,5) has 5 valence electrons, the highest among Na(1), Al(3), Si(4), and P(5).

q: Why did the discovery of noble gases completely break Newlands' Law of Octaves?
o: With noble gases inserted after halogens, every 9th element (not 8th) shared similar properties
e: Inserting the 8th group (noble gases) made properties repeat at the 9th element instead of the 8th.

q: Given elements X(2,8,1), Y(2,8,7), and Z(2,8,8), which two react to form an ionic compound and which stays unreactive?
o: X and Z react, Y unreactive
X and Y form ionic XY, while Z remains unreactive
e: X (Na) and Y (Cl) form ionic NaCl (XY), while Z (Ar, 2,8,8) has a complete octet and remains chemically inert.

q: Nitrogen (Z=7) and Phosphorus (Z=15) both belong to Group 15. Which one is MORE electronegative and why?
o: Nitrogen, because its smaller atomic size lets its nucleus attract bonding electrons more strongly
e: Electronegativity decreases down a group as atomic size increases; hence smaller Nitrogen attracts electrons more strongly than Phosphorus.

q: Elements X (Z=13) and Y (Z=16) lie in which period and form what compound together?
e: Both have 3 shells (Period 3); valency 3 for X and valency 2 for Y yields X2Y3 (Al2S3).

q: Among the first 20 elements (Z = 1 to 20), how many noble gases are present?
e: Helium (2), Neon (10), and Argon (18) are the three noble gases within Z = 1 to 20.

q: In the Modern Periodic Table, the Period number of an element is strictly equal to:
o: Number of occupied electron shells in its atom
e: The period number equals the number of electron shells occupied in the neutral atom.

q: Among Li, Be, Na, and Mg, which pair loses TWO valence electrons to form dipositive ions (M²⁺)?
e: Beryllium and Magnesium both belong to Group 2 with 2 valence electrons.

q: Identify the Group 14 pair consisting of the Period 2 non-metal showing highest catenation and the Period 3 semiconductor metalloid below it:
e: Carbon (Z=6) sits above Silicon (Z=14) in Group 14.

q: Elements P (Z=12) and Q (Z=16) belong to Period 3. How do their atomic radii compare?
o: Atomic size of P (Mg) is larger than Q (S)
e: Across Period 3, increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons inward, so P (left) has a larger radius than Q (right).

q: Across Group 2 elements Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, which element has the strongest metallic character?
e: Metallic character increases down a group, making Barium (at the bottom of stable Group 2 metals) the most metallic.

q: Neutral chlorine atom (Z=17) gains one electron to form chloride ion Cl⁻. Does the number of electron shells change?
o: Shell count stays 3 (2, 8, 8), while inter-electronic repulsion slightly enlarges the ionic radius
e: The gained electron enters the same 3rd shell (giving 2, 8, 8), keeping shell count at 3 while increasing radius slightly.

q: Why is the radius of a Na⁺ cation smaller than that of a neutral Na atom?
o: Loss of the entire 3rd valence shell (leaving 2 shells) and stronger effective nuclear pull on remaining 10 electrons
e: Losing the outermost electron removes the 3rd shell completely, leaving 11 protons pulling 10 electrons in 2 shells more tightly.

q: Which period in the Modern Periodic Table contains only 2 elements, BOTH of which are non-metals?
e: Period 1 consists solely of Hydrogen and Helium, both non-metals.

q: An atom has 5 electrons in its L shell. Identify its group, period, and identity:
e: K=2 and L=5 gives Z=7 (Nitrogen), located in Period 2 and Group 15.

q: In Group 17 (halogens), identify the elements existing as gas, liquid, and solid at room temperature respectively:
e: Down Group 17, increasing intermolecular attractions change the physical state from gases (F2, Cl2) to liquid (Br2) to solid (I2).

q: Which element forms an oxide whose aqueous solution will NOT turn red litmus blue?
e: Na, K, and Ca form basic metal oxides, whereas non-metal sulphur forms acidic oxides that turn blue litmus red.

Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both A and R are true, and R directly explains why both form H2X hydrides.

q:
Assertion (A): A Na⁺ cation is larger in size than a neutral Na atom.
Reason (R): A neutral Na atom loses one electron to form Na⁺.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: A is false because losing the 3rd shell makes Na⁺ smaller than Na; R is true.

q: From a periodic excerpt showing Period 2 (B, C, N, O) and Period 3 (Al, Si, P, S), identify the elements forming an amphoteric oxide and an acidic oxide:
o: Al (amphoteric Al2O3) and S or N (acidic oxides)
e: Aluminium forms amphoteric Al2O3, while non-metals like Sulphur and Nitrogen form acidic oxides.

q: Element "E" has electronic configuration 2, 8, 5. Which statement about E is INCORRECT?
o: It is a non-metal (Phosphorus) with valency 3
It forms a basic ionic chloride ECl
e: Phosphorus (2,8,5) is a non-metal forming covalent halides (PCl3/PCl5), NOT a basic ionic chloride ECl.

q: In Group 1, X is in Period 2 (Li), Y in Period 3, and Z in Period 4. Which element loses its valence electron MOST easily?
o: Z (having 4 shells, the valence electron is farthest from the nucleus)
e: Z (Potassium, Period 4) has the largest atomic size, weakest nuclear hold on its valence electron, and loses it most readily.

q: Elements with Z = 12 and Z = 17 react together. What are their names, bond type, and formula?
e: Magnesium (Z=12) and Chlorine (Z=17) combine via electron transfer to form ionic MgCl2.

q: Moving down Group 14 from C (non-metal) → Si, Ge (metalloids) → Sn, Pb (metals) demonstrates that:
o: Metallic character increases down a group
e: Increasing atomic size down a group makes electron loss easier, progressively shifting non-metals to metalloids and metals.

q: Among P (Z=3), Q (Z=11), R (Z=12), and S (Z=19), which element belongs to a DIFFERENT group from the other three?
e: P, Q, and S each have 1 valence electron (Group 1), whereas R (2,8,2) has 2 valence electrons (Group 2).

q: Mendeleev predicted the oxide formula of Eka-aluminium as E2O3. What is the actual formula of Gallium oxide?
e: Gallium is in Group 13 (like Al) and forms Ga2O3, matching Mendeleev's prediction exactly.

q: An atom X has only K and L shells with 6 electrons in the L shell. Identify X and its group:
e: K=2, L=6 gives Z=8 (Oxygen), in Period 2 and Group 16.

q: Elements X (Z=10), Y (Z=18), and Z (Z=2) are placed together in the same column. What is their common valency?
e: Helium, Neon, and Argon have completely filled outermost shells, so their valency is zero.

q: How is "atomic radius" defined for an isolated atom?
o: Distance between the centre of the nucleus and the outermost electron shell
e: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of the nucleus to the outermost shell, typically measured in picometres (pm).

q: What is the approximate atomic radius of a Hydrogen atom as given in NCERT?
e: According to NCERT, the atomic radius of a hydrogen atom is 37 pm.

q: An atom X contains 15 protons and 16 neutrons in its nucleus. Which number determines its exact position in the Modern Periodic Table?
e: Modern Periodic Table places elements strictly by atomic number (number of protons = 15, Phosphorus).

q: Across Period 2, what happens to the metallic nature of Lithium and Beryllium versus Carbon, Nitrogen, and Oxygen?
o: Li and Be are metals, B is a metalloid, and C, N, O, F, Ne are non-metals
Only O and F are non-metals
e: In Period 2, Li and Be are metals, B is a metalloid, and C, N, O, F, Ne are non-metals.

q: Why does Calcium (Z=20) resemble Magnesium (Z=12) above it and Strontium (Z=38) below it?
o: All three belong to Group 2 and have 2 valence electrons
e: Mg, Ca, and Sr all have 2 valence electrons in their outermost shell (Group 2).

q: Which of the following was a major achievement of Mendeleev's periodic table?
o: He predicted undiscovered elements via gaps and accommodated noble gases later without disturbing existing order
e: Mendeleev's key triumphs were predicting new elements via gaps and accommodating noble gases cleanly when discovered.

q: Elements A(9), B(17), and C(35) belong to Group 17. Select the completely accurate statement comparing their radius, reactivity, and electronegativity:
o: Radius A > B > C; reactivity C > B > A
Radius increases A < B < C, whereas reactivity and electronegativity decrease A > B > C
All properties increase A < B < C
e: Going down Group 17, shells increase so radius A < B < C, whereas attraction for an incoming electron decreases so reactivity & electronegativity follow A > B > C.

q: Element X belongs to Group 2, Period 3 and element Y belongs to Group 15, Period 2. What is the formula of the compound formed between X and Y?
e: X (Mg, Group 2) has valency 2 and Y (N, Group 15) has valency 3; cross-multiplying gives X3Y2 (Mg3N2).

q: Moving from left to right across Period 3 (Na → Mg → Al → P → S → Cl), how does the pH of aqueous solutions of their highest oxides change?
o: Decreases (strongly basic ~14 via amphoteric to strongly acidic ~1)
e: Oxide solutions transition from strongly basic NaOH (high pH) through amphoteric Al2O3 to strongly acidic oxyacids like H2SO4 (low pH).

q: Which set of three atomic numbers does NOT represent elements of the same vertical group in the Modern Periodic Table?
e: While 8 and 16 are Group 16 elements, Z=24 is Chromium (Group 6); the next Group 16 element is Selenium (16 + 18 = 34).

q: Across a period from left to right (e.g., Li to Ne), the energy required to remove an electron from the valence shell generally:
o: Increases, because shrinking size and higher nuclear charge bind valence electrons more tightly
e: Smaller atomic radius and higher nuclear charge hold outermost electrons tightly, increasing ionisation energy across a period.

q: Arrange F (Z=9), O (Z=8), and N (Z=7) in INCREASING order of atomic radius:
e: Across Period 2, atomic size decreases from N to O to F, giving increasing order F < O < N.

q: Elements B (Z=5) and Al (Z=13) belong to the same group. Identify the group number and their common valency:
e: Both B (2,3) and Al (2,8,3) have 3 valence electrons, placing them in Group 13 (10 + 3) with valency 3.

q: An element M forms a sulphate M2(SO4)3. What will be the formulas of its phosphate and nitrate respectively?
e: From M2(SO4)3, valency of M is +3. With PO4³⁻ it forms MPO4 (3:3 → 1:1) and with NO3⁻ it forms M(NO3)3.

q: Compare the isotopes ¹⁶O and ¹⁸O with respect to electronic configuration and valency:
o: Both have identical electronic configuration (2, 6) and valency (2)
e: Isotopes differ only in neutron count; both have 8 protons and 8 electrons, giving identical configuration (2,6) and valency 2.

q: What are the periodic interval "magic numbers" (2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32) in the Modern Periodic Table actually equal to?
o: Total number of elements in Periods 1 through 6 respectively
e: Adding 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32 advances down Group 1 from H(1) to Li(3), Na(11), K(19), Rb(37), Cs(55), Fr(87)—the exact period lengths.

q: Although nuclear charge increases sharply down a group, why does atomic size STILL increase instead of shrinking?
o: The effect of adding new principal electron shells outweighs the increase in nuclear charge
e: Adding a new shell places valence electrons much farther out and inner shells shield nuclear charge, increasing radius.

q: Compare the reactivity of Group 2 metals Be, Mg, and Ca with water:
o: Ca reacts with cold water, Mg reacts with hot water/steam, and Be does not react with water/steam
Mg reacts violently with cold water
e: Reactivity increases down Group 2: Be is unreactive with water, Mg needs hot water/steam, and Ca reacts with cold water.

q: Element X (2, 8, 3) and element Y (2, 6) combine to form a stable ionic compound. Identify its formula:
e: X has valency 3 (Al) and Y has valency 2 (O); cross-multiplying yields X2Y3 (Al2O3).

q: Why is Magnesium (Z=12) larger in atomic radius than Sulphur (Z=16) and Chlorine (Z=17) even though Cl has more electrons?
o: All three have 3 shells, but higher nuclear charge in S (16) and Cl (17) pulls the 3rd shell inward more strongly
e: With equal shell count (3), higher nuclear charge in S and Cl contracts the outer shell compared to Mg.

q: Among elements with configurations (i) 2,8,1 (ii) 2,8,7 (iii) 2,4 (iv) 2,8,2, which predominantly forms COVALENT compounds?
e: With 4 valence electrons, carbon (2,4) avoids forming C⁴⁺ or C⁴⁻ and shares electrons covalently.

q: In Period 3 oxides (Na2O, MgO, Al2O3, SiO2, P2O5, SO3, Cl2O7), what is the valency of each Period 3 element WITH RESPECT TO OXYGEN?
o: Increases continuously from 1 to 7 across the period
e: While valency relative to hydrogen peaks at 4 and drops to 1, maximum valency towards oxygen rises continuously from 1 (Na2O) to 7 (Cl2O7)!

q: Element X (Z=9) reacts with element Y (Z=19). Identify the electron donor, electron acceptor, and compound formula:
o: Y (K: 2,8,8,1) is donor, X (F: 2,7) is acceptor, forming ionic YX (KF)
e: Potassium (Y) donates 1 electron to Fluorine (X) to form ionic potassium fluoride (KF).

q: Among Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Arsenic (As) of Group 15, which element is a metalloid?
e: In Group 15, N and P are non-metals, As and Sb are metalloids, and Bi is a metal.

q: Element X forms ionic chloride XCl2. What is the formula of its sulphide when reacting with Sulphur (Group 16)?
e: Since X has +2 charge and S has -2 charge, they combine 1:1 to form XS.

q: Both Neon atom (Z=10) and Mg²⁺ ion (Z=12) have 10 electrons (2, 8). Which has a smaller radius and why?
o: Mg²⁺ is smaller because 12 protons pull the 10 electrons more strongly than 10 protons in Neon
e: Among isoelectronic species (10 electrons each), greater nuclear charge (12 protons in Mg²⁺ vs 10 in Ne) shrinks the radius more.

q: Why did Mendeleev reverse the atomic mass order for pairs like Cobalt (58.9) before Nickel (58.7) or Tellurium (127.6) before Iodine (126.9)?
o: To ensure elements with similar chemical properties fell into the same vertical group
e: Mendeleev prioritised grouping elements with similar properties over strict atomic mass order in a few cases.

q: Among P(4), Q(12), R(17), and S(18), identify which pair forms an ionic compound and which element has a basic oxide:
o: P and Q ionic; R basic
Q (Mg) and R (Cl) form ionic QR2, and Q forms a basic oxide
e: Magnesium (Q) and Chlorine (R) form ionic MgCl2 (QR2), and MgO is basic.

q: Why is Hydrogen a gas at room temperature despite being placed above solid alkali metals (Li, Na, K) in Group 1?
o: Being non-metallic, hydrogen exists as discrete covalent H2 molecules with weak intermolecular forces
e: Unlike alkali metals with metallic bonding, hydrogen forms discrete covalent H2 molecules with very weak intermolecular forces.

q: Groups 13 to 18 on the right side of the periodic table (housing all non-metals except H and metalloids) contain elements of groups:
o: Groups 13–18 (p-block: metals, metalloids, non-metals, noble gases)
e: Groups 1–2 hold active metals, 3–12 hold transition metals, while Groups 13–18 hold metals, metalloids, non-metals, and noble gases.

q: Element X has atomic number 15 (Phosphorus). Find the atomic numbers of the element directly ABOVE it and directly to its RIGHT:
e: Directly above 2,8,5 (15) is 2,5 (Z=7, Nitrogen); directly to the right in Period 3 is Z=16 (Sulphur).

q: Moving across a period atomic radius shrinks from Group 1 to Group 17, yet why does the Group 18 noble gas have a slightly larger apparent radius?
o: Completely filled octet causes strong inter-electronic repulsion (and radius is measured as van der Waals radius)
e: Noble gases do not form covalent bonds so their larger van der Waals radius is measured, combined with strong inter-electronic repulsion in filled shells.

q: Across Period 3 (Na to Cl), which element is most electropositive and which is most electronegative?
o: Cl most electropositive, Na most electronegative
Na is most electropositive (metal) and Cl is most electronegative (non-metal)
e: Sodium on the far left loses electrons most easily (most electropositive), while Chlorine on the right attracts electrons most strongly (most electronegative).

q: In Newlands' Octaves, Lithium (1st), Sodium (8th), and Potassium (15th) fell in the same note column. How are they placed in the Modern Periodic Table?
o: They still fall in the exact same vertical column (Group 1) across Periods 2, 3, and 4
e: For light elements up to Calcium before noble gases were known, octave grouping matched modern Group 1 (Li, Na, K).

q: Which pair of metals belongs to Group 2 (Alkaline earth metals) rather than Group 1 (Alkali metals)?
e: Group 2 comprises Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, and Ra—the alkaline earth metals.

q: Element X forms sulphate XSO4 and is located in Group 2, Period 4. Identify X and its valence shell:
e: Group 2, Period 4 has configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 (Z=20, Calcium), with 2 valence electrons in the 4th (N) shell.
